A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGLS study. All 16 pages of v3 and 18 pages of v4, including appendices, support comparison. The observable formatting errors in v4 do not prevent matching the scientific content.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original compute-matched pretraining and domain-adaptive code experiments. The appendices include original ablations and repeated-run results.

after.justification: Original pretraining results remain, and Tables 9–11 add retention measurements, a freezing ablation, and a reversed-curriculum experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same curriculum mixtures, randomly initialized layer additions, initialization with earlier layers frozen, and subsequent full-model tuning. The new no-freeze and reversed-curriculum variants are diagnostic ablations; the proposed CGLS procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora, domains, and benchmark task coverage remain the same. GPT-2 gains LAMBADA results, but that task was already evaluated with Llama. The new retention analyses reuse existing DCLM curriculum subsets.

E2.justification: The four principal baselines remain. GPT-2 Table 1 drops CGLS (Simple), while the GPT-2 Pile breakdown replaces the Simple and N1=3 variants with MIDAS and layer-scaling-only comparisons, although those baselines already appeared in Table 1.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 revises the GPT-2 budget from 700M tokens to FLOPs equivalent to 2.5B full-depth training tokens. GPT-2 evaluation now includes LAMBADA in the trained-model averages. New appendix protocols measure final-model perplexity on curriculum subsets and separately remove freezing or reverse curriculum order.

E4.justification: New Sections A.6–A.8 test retention of early distributions, the contribution of freezing, and the importance of curriculum direction through Tables 9–11. These substantially extend mechanism testing beyond the retained depth/budget sweeps, classifier substitution, and stagewise performance analyses.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same three training runs per method, numerical results, and standard-error reporting. No changed run counts or new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: GPT-2 Table 1 and Pile results are replaced under the larger budget. CGLS perplexity changes from 34.33 to 29.31, while the randomized baseline changes from 37.51 to 27.93, reversing their relative ordering. Tables 9–11 add retention and ablation outcomes; Table 11 reports 32.52% average accuracy for reversed curriculum versus 39.08% for CGLS. The Llama results in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The curriculum-mixture equation, parameter-transfer initialization, and FLOP approximation remain unchanged. Explaining the concatenation symbol adds clarity without revising mathematical reasoning; neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution framing, and conclusion retain the central claim that coordinated curriculum and depth growth improves compute-matched pretraining across the tested scales and domain shift. The updated GPT-2 numerical example leaves that contribution's meaning and scope unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 adds a stability–plasticity interpretation of the freezing ablation and qualifies the synchronization argument by acknowledging that curriculum reversal is a substantial intervention. It also presents GPT-2 as a capacity-limited proof of concept and extends the perplexity/downstream-performance discrepancy to both model scales.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains full-depth-equivalent token accounting and resampling exhausted early-stage mixtures without additional unique data. Appendix A.1 clarifies the runtime comparison. These disclosures do not establish a changed Llama training procedure; the hardware, optimization settings, and reported runtimes remain the same.

R1.justification: The cited studies and research-positioning arguments remain the same. Changes to references such as LayerDrop, H-Nets, and Beyond Random Sampling update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify compute accounting and revise the GPT-2 results discussion, alongside new appendix subsections. Conference information, conflict disclosure, acknowledgements, and an impact statement are added. The main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds three appendix tables, simplifies Table 4, and revises the GPT-2 Pile plot and legend. Retained figures are renumbered or relocated. The page-3 schematic remains, but its explanatory caption is replaced by raw BibTeX and its figure references become unresolved question marks.

improvement.justification: The added freezing and reversal controls, retention measurements, and clearer compute accounting provide a limited net improvement in empirical support and transparency. Reporting defects temper these gains: v4 corrupts the method-figure caption, introduces inconsistent averages such as Table 10's baseline value, and retains an introductory claim of GPT-2 perplexity gains that its revised Table 1 contradicts.
